protocol: Cross-person EEG object centers as a training teacher for a single-person 12-way object readout. Register before evaluating this candidate. This experiment uses no image embeddings or pixels and no within-object photo correspondences across participants.
split: Use precisely the 416 fitting/96 evaluation objects already frozen for a different photo-level analysis. Other studies have inspected this generic set. No selecting ranks, blending weights or analyses from the results of this new model.
baseline: For each person, fit the native 17-channel 96-dimensional Fisher model on 4160 four-trial generic waveforms. Query and all labeled supports at inference use this person's four-trial EEG alone. Score each class by the native standardized cosine to its eight-support arithmetic mean.
teacher: Reduce the other two people's 10 training EEGs to one object center per person in their own separately fitted training Fisher spaces. Subtract each person's training session-pair mean center, divide by coordinate training SD, and concatenate the two teachers with equal weight. Fit reduced-rank ridge from the recipient's standardized native training centers to these target coordinates. Rank 64, ridge 0.5 times the average centered source Gram diagonal. Use the top singular values as amplitudes. Mix recipient native and teacher-space standardized prototype cosine scores at equal weight.
controls: Native 96D Fisher on the same training classes. Sham teachers use the same dimensions and pipeline but reassign each donor's training class centers without fixed points within exact joint recipient/donor recording-session-pair strata; seed 260532. Self teacher uses the recipient's own session-centered class centers with the same rank, ridge, source dimension and equal score mixture.
primary: For each of three repeats permute the same 96 evaluation classes using seed 260533, taking sliding groups of twelve every four positions; independently permute the ten photos per object, and hold out successive pairs across five folds. Each evaluation object receives 90 decisions per person. Every arm shares the folds, competitors and query rows. No fit or normalization across held-out objects, except the legal eight supports per class and within-query normalization across the twelve scores.
session_check: Separately show 30 decisions per held-out object: three deterministically seeded groups of 11 competitors sharing that recipient's exact two recording sessions, with ten held-out query appearances each. Session labels are used only to assemble this diagnostic evaluation, and never supplied to inference.
uncertainty: Use 10000 bootstraps of the 96 objects sampled jointly for all people and all arms, seed 260534. Sum participant hits within each object first. Per-person differences are descriptive. Objects, not repeat episodes or people, are the resampling unit.
advance: Only if the lower 95 percent paired class-bootstrap bound versus both native and session-matched sham is strictly above zero on the primary evaluation may the frozen candidate be evaluated on the previously studied fourth target panel. Report the self-teacher and same-session tests separately regardless. On passing refit on all 512 generic training objects, use frozen fourth-panel folds with eight personally measured EEG supports, and verify that the native arm replays posterior baseline predictions exactly. Fourth-panel results are developmental.
